extraction_text: Yudhishthira and Bhima surrounded Ashvatthama from all sides.
Duryodhana, with Ashvatthama, charged at the Pandavas in battle.
Yudhishthira angrily sent groups of Ambashthas, Malavas, Vangas, Shibis, and Trikartas to the world of Death.
Bhima slaughtered fierce Kshatriyas from Abhisahas and Surasenas, covering the earth with bloody mud.
Arjuna sent many Yaudheyas, Arattas, and Madras to the world of Death with sharp arrows.
Drona, enraged, used the Wind God weapon in battle, destroying enemies like an irresistible wind scattering clouds.

attributes.effect: Destroyed enemies, caused Panchalas to flee

extraction_text: Arjuna and Bhima, with a large chariot force, suddenly surrounded the Kaurava army.
Bhima and Arjuna attacked Drona from both sides with torrents of arrows.
Srinjayas, Panchala warriors, Matsyas, and Somakas followed Arjuna and Bhima.
Many skilled Kaurava charioteers and a large army went to Drona's chariot.
The Kaurava army, slaughtered by Arjuna and afflicted by darkness and drowsiness, collapsed again.
Despite Drona and Duryodhana trying to stop them, warriors fled uncontrollably.
Hundreds of kings, overwhelmed by fear, abandoned chariots and horses, fleeing in all directions.
Satyaki, seeing Shalya wielding a large bow, told his charioteer to take him to Shalya, vowing to kill him or not return from battle.
Satyaki (Sātyaki) rides Sindhu horses to the battlefield, compared to Indra's celestial horses.
Satyaki charges at Bhurishravas (Bhūriśravas) on the battlefield.
Bhurishravas showers Satyaki with arrows, covering him like clouds covering the sun.
Satyaki counterattacks Bhurishravas with arrows from all directions.
Bhurishravas shoots sixty arrows into Satyaki's chest; Satyaki retaliates with arrows.
Both warriors, covered in blood and arrows, glare at each other as if burning with their gaze.

attributes.imagery: Like flowering trees, glowing with arrows

extraction_text: Bhurishravas breaks Satyaki's bow with a crescent-headed arrow.
Satyaki takes another powerful bow and shoots five arrows at Bhurishravas.
Satyaki cuts down Bhurishravas's golden flag with a crescent-headed arrow.
Satyaki breaks Bhurishravas's bow with a sharp horse-hoof arrow.
Bhima (Bhīma) shoots ten arrows at Bhurishravas to aid Satyaki.
Ghatotkacha (Ghaṭotkaca), Bhima's son, hurls a terrible iron bar at Bhurishravas's chest.
Bhurishravas smiles and splits the iron bar in two as it falls.
Satyaki broke the large iron bar into two pieces with his weapon.
Satyaki shot and broke Somadatta's bow with a crescent-headed arrow, then pierced his finger-guard with five arrows.
Satyaki killed Somadatta's four horses with four arrows.
Satyaki beheaded Somadatta's charioteer with a crescent-headed arrow.
Satyaki shot a sharp golden-feathered arrow that pierced Somadatta's chest, killing him.
Many warriors attacked Satyaki after seeing Somadatta killed.
Yudhishthira led an army against Drona's forces when he saw Satyaki covered in arrows.
Yudhishthira angrily routed the Kaurava army in front of Drona.
Drona, enraged by Yudhishthira routing his army, charged forward and shot seven arrows at Yudhishthira.
Drona cut Yudhishthira's flag and bow with arrows.
Yudhishthira took another bow and shot thousands of arrows at Drona, his horses, charioteer, flag, and chariot.
Drona was struck by arrows and fell unconscious on his chariot seat.
Drona regained consciousness, became furious, and used the Vayuastra (wind god weapon).
Yudhishthira calmly countered Drona's divine weapon with another divine weapon.
Krishna advised Yudhishthira to stop fighting Drona because Drona was trying to capture him, and someone else was destined to kill Drona the next day.
Yudhishthira went to where Bhima was fighting Duryodhana's forces and began killing Kaurava soldiers.
Drona took advantage of the night to slaughter Pandava and Panchala forces.
The horrific battle continues with darkness and dust covering the world, making warriors unable to see each other clearly.

attributes.supernatural_elements: Darkness and dust covering the battlefield

extraction_text: Warriors kill based on names, slaughtering men, horses, and elephants in the bloody battle.

extraction_text: Armies are slaughtered everywhere in the darkness and dust, fleeing in all directions.
Duryodhana commands the army commanders to reorganize all remaining troops.
Duryodhana forms a new battle formation with Drona at the front, Shalya at the rear, Ashvatthaman and Shakuni on the flanks, while Duryodhana himself protects the entire army.

attributes.relationships: Duryodhana as overall protector, Drona as vanguard, Shalya as rearguard

extraction_text: The army of the Pandavas (referred to as 'your army' in context) appeared extremely terrifying under various beams of light, like a great forest fire that dims the sun.
Sons of Pritha (Pandavas) ordered infantry to light torches throughout all armies.
Soldiers placed seven lamps on each elephant, ten on each chariot, two on each horse, plus on chariot wings, tails, and banners.
They arranged numerous torch-bearing warriors around the entire army - left, right, front, back, middle, and surroundings.
Infantry mixed with countless elephant riders, charioteers, and cavalry throughout all armies, with some standing in the middle holding lit torches to illuminate the army of Pandu's sons.
The radiant army made the glittering army (Kauravas) even more brilliant, like blazing fire under bright sunlight.
The light from both armies illuminated sky, earth, and all directions, making both armies clearly visible.
The light shooting into sky startled all gods, Gandharvas, Yakshas, Asuras, Siddhas, and celestial maidens, who came together to witness.

attributes.action: Divine beings gather to observe battle

extraction_text: The battlefield resembled heaven due to gathering of gods, Gandharvas, Yakshas, Asura lords, celestial maidens, and groups of fallen heroes about to ascend to heaven.

attributes.supernatural_elements: Mortal battlefield taking on divine qualities

extraction_text: The army filled with chariots, horses, and elephants under torchlight, with angry warriors, fallen or galloping horses everywhere, resembled armies of gods and Asuras.
In the night, fierce battle raged among kings - flying javelins like gusts of wind, massive chariots like clouds, sounds like thunder, weapons like torrential rain, blood forming floods.
In this battle, the great-souled Brahmin leader Drona burned the Pandavas like a great fire, like the scorching midday sun at end of rainy season.

attributes.relationships: Drona as Kaurava commander fighting Pandavas
attributes.description: Drona's destructive power compared to natural forces

extraction_text: After the dusty, dark world regained light, heroes attacked each other, eager to kill.
They held javelins, sharp swords, and other weapons, encountering each other on battlefield, glaring with hatred.
All directions illuminated by thousands of lamps, earth like starry night sky.
Under hundreds of burning torches, battlefield resembled earth burning at world's destruction.
All directions illuminated by omnipresent lamps, like forest full of fireflies on rainy season night.

attributes.description: Natural comparison to complete the scene

Duryodhana explained his strategic reasoning: protecting Drona would lead to victory over the Somakas and Srinjayas, after which Ashvatthaman could kill Dhrishtadyumna.

A terrible night battle erupted between the two armies desiring victory.
Arjuna hurled various weapons at the Kaurava army, and the Kauravas reciprocated against Arjuna.
Dronacharya (son of Bharadvaja) and Ashvatthama (son of Drona) covered the Srinjayas and King of Panchala with straight arrows.

Satyaki (grandson of Shini) showered arrows in all directions, and Pritha (Kuru descendant) charged at him.
Nakula (son of Pandu) attempted to reach Dronacharya but was intercepted by Karna (son of Surya).
Bhima charged forward like Death with gaping mouth, and Duryodhana personally advanced to meet him.
Shakuni (son of Subala) swiftly intercepted the skilled warrior Sahadeva.
Shikhandi charged in his chariot and was blocked in battle by Kripa (son of Sharadvata).
Yudhamanyu charged in his chariot drawn by peacock-like horses and was vigorously blocked by Duhshasana.
Ghatotkacha (son of Bhima) charged forward, and Ashvatthama intercepted him to uphold his father's honor.

extraction_text: Dhrishtadyumna (Prince of Panchala) intercepted the great archer Dronacharya as he excitedly slew enemies in battle.
Other great warriors of the five Pandavas launched attacks, and the Kaurava chariot warriors provided strong resistance.
Hundreds and thousands of elephant warriors rapidly charged against each other and fought fiercely.
Many warhorses charge and clash like winged mountains, and cavalrymen engage in battle with spears, javelins, and swords, shouting as they fight.
Large groups of warriors engage in a melee, striking each other with clubs, maces, and various weapons.
Kritavarma, son of Hridika, filled with rage, blocks Yudhishthira, son of Dharma, like a shore blocking the raging sea.
Yudhishthira shoots five arrows at Kritavarma, then twenty more, shouting 'Stand! Stand!'
Kritavarma, enraged, severs Yudhishthira's bow with a crescent-headed arrow and shoots seven more arrows at him.
Yudhishthira takes another bow and shoots ten arrows hitting Kritavarma's arms and chest.
Kritavarma, trembling and furious, shoots seven arrows at Yudhishthira.
Yudhishthira (son of Pritha/Kunti) breaks Kritavarma's bow and leather guard, then shoots five sharpened arrows that pierce his gold-inlaid armor and embed in the ground.
Kritavarma quickly takes another bow and shoots sixty arrows at Yudhishthira and nine at his charioteer.
Yudhishthira puts down his bow and throws a snake-like, gold-inlaid spear that pierces Kritavarma's right arm and enters the ground.
Yudhishthira picks up his bow again and covers Kritavarma with many straight arrows.
Kritavarma, the heroic and excellent chariot warrior of the Vrishni clan, makes Yudhishthira lose his horses, charioteer, and chariot in less than a blink.
Yudhishthira, the eldest Pandava, takes up sword and shield in battle, but Kritavarma destroys them with sharp arrows.
Yudhishthira takes a powerful gold-shafted spear and swiftly throws it at Kritavarma.
Kritavarma, quick-handed, smiles and breaks the speeding spear thrown by Yudhishthira into two pieces.
Kritavarma, furious, showers Yudhishthira with hundreds of arrows, piercing his armor with many sharp arrows.
Yudhishthira's armor, shattered by Kritavarma's arrows, falls to the battlefield like countless stars falling from the sky.
Yudhishthira, with bow broken, chariot destroyed, and armor shattered under arrow strikes, immediately withdraws from the battlefield.
The mighty Kritavarma, having defeated Yudhishthira, continues to guard Drona's chariot wheel.
